correctness.rationale: Exact enumerative proof: character-2 Euler identity reduces cubic geometric smoothness to the zero-dimensionality of the ideal of three homogeneous partial quadrics. SymPy's exact finite-field Gröbner basis runs over all 1023 nonzero cubics, finds 336 smooth; complete coset-extension of all subspaces yields 5544 pencils, 864 smooth nets and no dimension-four systems. Enumerating 168 full invertible coordinate transforms yields 8 disjoint orbits of 3×8+5×168=864, with stabilizers 21 or 1. Every one of eight coefficient-mask bases and all member rational-point spectra are recomputed. Direct derivative scans through F16 agree on all 687 singular masks but are supplementary. Standalone source was executed and final output was SMOOTH_NET_CLASSIFICATION_PASS 336 5544 864 8. No infinite family extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Original assessed statement is the complete count 864 and eight PGL3(F2) coordinate orbits (three with stabilizer 21, five trivial) of geometric-smooth cubic nets. AGR (2022) proves existence and maximum projective dimension, but not counts or orbit decomposition; AGR (2024) studies geometric irreducibility, not the exact smooth-net census. Berg (1998) concerns characteristic numbers over algebraically closed characteristic-two fields, not binary rational net orbits. Direct searches of current mathematical records found no covering classification. Residual risk of unindexed enumerations is explicit.

value.rationale: AGR's natural extremal-smoothness question already proves existence/maximal dimension of F2-smooth cubic nets; the number of distinct maximal nets and moduli under rational coordinate changes is a separate natural classification problem. The 864-count and eight-class decomposition reveal three nets with stabilizer order 21 versus five asymmetric classes with trivial stabilizers; distinct coordinate types share identical multisets of member point counts, so mere existence and such coarse invariants are insufficient. A complete finite-field moduli census is a substantive invariant, not an arbitrary parameter slice or routine restatement of the existence theorem.
